subtitle: Glaciers and radiating valleys
notes: Rainier is a stratovolcano and the highest peak in the Cascades, at about 4,392 m. It carries more glacier ice than any other peak in the contiguous United States.
Glaciers and rivers flow outward from the summit in every direction. The Carbon, White, Nisqually, Puyallup, and Cowlitz drainages start on its slopes.
Elevation is drawn as filled bands. Glaciers mapped in OpenStreetMap are left as empty space, so the ice reads as the shape of the mountain.
